JACOBIAN ELLIPTIC FUNCTIONS AND THETA FUNCTIONS (p.579)
FIGURE 16.5. Logarithmic derivatives of theta functions. \frac{d}{du}\ln\vartheta_s(u), \frac{d}{du}\ln\vartheta_n(u), m=\tfrac12
16.37. Expression as Infinite Products
q=q(m),\ v=\pi u/(2K)
16.37.1  \vartheta_s(u)=\left(\tfrac{16q}{mm_1}\right)^{1/6}\sin v\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} (1-2q^{2n}\cos2v+q^{4n})
16.37.2  \vartheta_c(u)=\left(\tfrac{16qm_1^{1/2}}{m}\right)^{1/6}\cos v\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} (1+2q^{2n}\cos2v+q^{4n})
16.37.3  \vartheta_d(u)=\left(\tfrac{mm_1}{16q}\right)^{1/12}\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} (1+2q^{2n-1}\cos2v+q^{4n-2})
16.37.4  \vartheta_n(u)=\left(\tfrac{m}{16qm_1^2}\right)^{1/12}\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} (1-2q^{2n-1}\cos2v+q^{4n-2})
16.38. Expression as Infinite Series
Let v=\pi u/(2K)
16.38.1  \vartheta_s(u)=\left[\tfrac{2\pi q^{1/2}}{m^{1/2}m_1^{1/2}K}\right]^{1/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^nq^{n(n+1)}\sin(2n+1)v
16.38.2  \vartheta_c(u)=\left[\tfrac{2\pi q^{1/2}}{m^{1/2}K}\right]^{1/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} q^{n(n+1)}\cos(2n+1)v
16.38.3  \vartheta_d(u)=\left[\tfrac{\pi}{2K}\right]^{1/2}\{1+2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} q^{n^2}\cos2nv\}
16.38.4  \vartheta_n(u)=\left[\tfrac{\pi}{2m_1^{1/2}K}\right]^{1/2}\{1+2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (-1)^nq^{n^2}\cos2nv\}
16.38.5  (2K/\pi)^{1/2}=1+2q+2q^4+2q^9+\cdots=\vartheta_3(0,q)
16.38.6  (2K'/\pi)^{1/2}=1+2q_1+2q_1^4+2q_1^9+\cdots=\vartheta_3(0,q_1)
16.38.7  (2m^{1/2}K/\pi)^{1/2}=2q^{1/4}(1+q^2+q^6+q^{12}+q^{20}+\cdots)=\vartheta_2(0,q)
16.38.8  (2m_1^{1/2}K/\pi)^{1/2}=1-2q+2q^4-2q^9+\cdots=\vartheta_4(0,q).
Numerical Methods
16.39. Use and Extension of the Tables
Example 1. Calculate nc(1.99650|.64) to 4S. From Table 17.1, 1.99650=K+.001. From the table of principal terms nc\,u=-m_1^{-1/2}/(u-K)+\cdots,\ \mathrm{nc}(K+.001|.64)=\frac{-(.36)^{-1/2}}{.001}+\cdots=-\frac{10000}{6}+\cdots=-1667+\cdots, and since the next term is of order .001 this value -1667 is correct to at least 4S.
Example 2. Use the descending Landen transformation to calculate dn(.20|.19) to 6D. Here m=.19, m_1^{1/2}=.9 and so from 16.12.1 \mu=(1/19)^2, 1+\mu^{1/2}=20/19, v=.19. Also \mu^2=(1/19)^4=10^{-6}\times7.67 which is negligible. From 16.12.4 \mathrm{dn}(.20|.19)=.996253 (via dn[.19|(1/19)^2]=.999951 from 16.13.3).
Example 3. Use the ascending Landen transformation to calculate dn(.20|.81) to 5D. From 16.14.1 \mu=4(.9)/(1.9)^2=360/361,\ \mu_1=(1/19)^2,\ 1+\mu_1^{1/2}=20/19,\ v=(19/20)\times.20=.19,\ \mu_1^2 is negligible to 4D. Thus [continues on next page].
